items.descriptionHtml: <p>IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience of your workforce to AWS accounts and applications. You can now use optimistic locking for users and groups in the identity store, so that update and delete requests succeed only if the user or group hasn't changed since you last read it. This helps when multiple administrators or automated workflows modify the same user or group at nearly the same time, where previously one write could silently overwrite another.<br> <br> Each user and group now has a Revision value that changes every time the user's or group's attributes are modified, including through SCIM provisioning, Active Directory sync, or the IAM Identity Center console. Create, describe, update, and list operations return the current Revision, and you can pass it on a later UpdateUser, UpdateGroup, DeleteUser, or DeleteGroup request. The request succeeds only if the supplied Revision matches the current Revision. Otherwise, it returns a ConflictException, so your workflow can re-read the user or group and retry with the latest values.<br> <br> Providing a Revision is optional. Requests that omit it behave as before, so existing integrations continue to work without changes. Conditional requests are supported through the Identity Store API, not the SCIM endpoint. Group membership operations don't accept a Revision, and adding or removing members doesn't change the Revision of the user or the group. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost.<br> <br> To learn more about IAM Identity Center, visit the product detail page. To get started, see UpdateUser in the <a title="identity store update user API" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/IdentityStoreAPIReference/API_UpdateUser.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Identity Store API Reference</a>.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p><a href="https://aws.amazon.com/iam/roles-anywhere/">AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles Anywhere</a> now provides a plugin for the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-java/latest/developer-guide/home.html">AWS SDK for Java v2</a> that enables workloads running outside of AWS to obtain temporary AWS credentials directly within the Java application process. items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions. When you enable it, CloudFront adds the script tag for the AWS WAF JavaScript SDK to the HTML it serves, with no change to your application code, build process, or deployment. The SDK supplies the client-side signals used by three AWS WAF managed rule groups: Bot Control at the targeted inspection level, Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP), and Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP).<br> <br> Previously, supplying those signals required you to add a script tag to every page of every application you wanted to protect, and to maintain that tag across releases. For teams running many applications, or serving pages produced by systems they do not control, this created recurring work and a common source of misconfiguration, where a protection was enabled in AWS WAF but the client-side integration was missing. Enabling automatic SDK integration on the web ACL protecting your CloudFront distribution removes that per-application work.<br> <br> Automatic SDK integration is available for web ACLs that are used with Amazon CloudFront and contain at least one of those managed rule groups. You can configure it using the AWS Management Console, CLI, SDK, CDK, or CloudFormation. In the AWS WAF console, the setting appears with the managed rule group settings and is on by default for new web ACLs that you create with one of those rule group. When you create a web ACL programmatically, the setting is off by default. Web ACLs created before this release are unchanged.<br> <br> There is no additional charge for automatic SDK integration. For requirements, limitations, and Content Security Policy guidance, see <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-challenge-javascript-sdk-injection.html">Automatic SDK integration for CloudFront distributions</a> in the AWS WAF Developer Guide.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p>Amazon S3 Object Lock now supports variable retention, allowing you to apply write-once-read-many (WORM) protection to objects whose required retention period starts with a future event, such as a contract closing or an audit completing. You place an event hold with a retention duration on an object and S3 protects the object while the hold is in place. When you release the hold, S3 retains the object for the duration you specified. Unlike legal holds, which end protection immediately upon removal, event holds provide WORM compliance for the required retention period after the triggering event, so you can meet event-based retention requirements without retaining data longer than your policy requires.<br> <br> You can apply event holds to individual objects, configure them as a bucket default, or apply them at scale with S3 Batch Operations. New AWS IAM and bucket policy condition keys let you control who can set or release holds and enforce minimum or maximum hold durations. AWS CloudTrail logs all hold operations and S3 Inventory reports hold status across your buckets.<br> <br> Event holds for S3 Object Lock are available in all AWS Regions, including China Regions, at no additional charge. To learn more, read the <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/flexibly-control-amazon-s3-object-lock-retention-based-on-real-business-events" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">AWS Storage Blog post</a>, the <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/s3/features/object-lock/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">S3 Object Lock overview page</a>, and the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">S3 documentation</a>.&nbsp;This capability has been <a href="https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/whitepapers/compliance/Amazon-S3-Compliance-Assessment-2026.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">assessed by&nbsp;Cohasset Associates</a>&nbsp;for use in environments subject to SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511, and CFTC Regulation 1.31.</p>

items.descriptionHtml:
<p>Amazon Redshift now supports querying Amazon S3 data lake tables located in a different AWS Region. With enhanced VPC routing, data lake query traffic between Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift stays within your own VPC.&nbsp;Both capabilities are powered by the integrated data lake query engine that runs directly on the compute of RG provisioned and Serverless clusters. These features are aimed at enterprises with globally distributed data and at security-sensitive customers who need tight control over how their data travels.</p>
<p>With cross-Region support, you can use Amazon Redshift to query S3 data in another Region directly, without first copying or replicating it. This makes it easier to run global analytics, consolidate reporting across Regions, and query data that must remain in a specific Region for residency requirements. Cross-Region queries incur standard data transfer charges. Because the query engine runs on your cluster's compute, data moving between Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift flows entirely over your VPC when you use enhanced VPC routing, never over public networks. Regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, and government benefit from this feature as it keeps data lake queries within the network boundaries their compliance requirements demand.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both capabilities work with the integrated data lake query engine, which is available in all regions where RG provisioned and Serverless clusters are available. To learn more, see <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/spectrum-enhanced-vpc.html#spectrum-enhanced-vpc-integrated-engine"><u>Querying your data lake</u>&nbsp;tables with enhanced VPC routing</a>&nbsp;in the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/" style="background-color: rgb(255,255,255);">Amazon Redshift documentation</a>.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS Quick now includes enterprise guardrails, giving administrators configurable content safety and sensitive-information controls for user prompts. Administrators can apply guardrail policies to individual users or enterprise identity provider (IdP) groups or set a policy as the account default.
